docs.title: NereidAI
docs.text:
Navigate the sea of data — from devices, to models, to edge intelligence.

An end-to-end, air-gapped, multi-silicon AIoT platform. IoT connectivity and AI intelligence in one closed loop — private by design.

Explore the suite Architecture

docs.title: The closed loop
docs.text:
NereidAI ships as a suite of focused products; each can be deployed standalone, and together they form one unified platform. A thin suite layer ties them together without absorbing their domain logic.

flowchart LR
    subgraph FIELD["Site / field"]
        DEV["cameras · sensors · robots"] --> EDGE["NE · Edge\ncollect data · run AI inference"]
    end
    FORGE["NF · Forge — the model factory\nannotate → train/fine-tune → quantize →\nmulti-silicon export → evaluate → register"]
    HORIZON["NH · Horizon\nmodel & app rollout (OTA)"]
    LINK["NL · Link\ningest · rules · alerts · dashboards"]

    EDGE -->|data / feedback| FORGE
    LINK -->|datasets & telemetry| FORGE
    FORGE -->|versioned models| HORIZON
    HORIZON -->|OTA models / apps| EDGE
    EDGE -->|inference events / telemetry| LINK

The loop has two halves that meet in Forge: the IoT half brings field data in (Edge, Link) and acts on results; the AI half turns that data into models (Forge) and ships them back to run at the edge (Horizon, Edge). Models improve from real telemetry, on the next iteration — with no mandatory cloud.

  • Private by design

    Fully offline / air-gapped delivery with no mandatory call-home. Data, training and inference all stay inside the customer perimeter.

  • From CNNs to large models

    One factory for classic vision models (detection / classification / segmentation) and large models — VLM-assisted labeling plus LLM / VLM fine-tuning and serving.

  • Multi-silicon → edge inference

    Export one trained model across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel, ARM, Ascend, SOPHGO, MetaX, Enflame and Rockchip, then run low-latency CV or VLM inference on the gateway.

  • Embodied & physical AI roadmap

    Take models off the screen and onto robots — NereidFleet orchestrates wheeled AMRs, quadrupeds and humanoids over ROS 2 / Open-RMF, toward vision-language-action and physical-AI workloads.

  • Massive device access, in real time

    Multi-protocol ingress (MQTT / HTTP / CoAP), a rule engine, alerting and dashboards — every change pushed over WebSocket, no polling.

  • Edge autonomy on flaky links

    Field gateways keep working while the WAN is down: local autonomy plus store-and-forward buffering that safely replays telemetry on reconnect.

  • Offline distribution at scale

    NereidHorizon rolls out Edge itself, apps and models to thousands of remote nodes — policy-driven, bandwidth-aware OTA with offline reconciliation.

  • One AIoT closed loop

    Field data → models → OTA rollout → edge inference → telemetry feedback: IoT connectivity and AI intelligence in a single loop, no mandatory cloud.

Apache-2.0 community edition · enterprise LTS, SLAs, hardening and turnkey private delivery — see Community vs Enterprise.

docs.title: From data to edge intelligence
docs.text:
The AI journey is a first-class path, not a side feature:

# Stage What happens Product 1 Collect Cameras, sensors and robots feed images, video and time-series data from the field. Edge, Link 2 Annotate Datasets are versioned; vision-language models (Florence-2, Qwen-VL) pre-label for human review. Forge 3 Train / fine-tune Kubeflow pipelines train classic vision models or fine-tune LLMs / VLMs (LLaMA-Factory) on the customer's own data. Forge 4 Optimize & export Quantize / compile (NNCF, OpenVINO, TensorRT, vLLM) and export for the target silicon. Forge 5 Evaluate & register Quality and benchmark metrics — including LLM-as-a-judge — gate each version; approved models enter the registry. Forge 6 Run at the edge Models roll out over the air and run as low-latency CV or VLM inference on gateways and devices. Horizon, Edge 7 Monitor & feed back Inference events and telemetry drive rules, alerts and the next training round. Link, Forge

The same loop powers the commercial solutions — smart-manufacturing inspection, video/image analytics (NereidSentinel) and medical insights (NereidMedical).

docs.title: Toward embodied & physical AI
docs.text: The next step beyond sensing and analytics is acting in the physical world. NereidFleet (currently Tech Preview) already orchestrates heterogeneous embodied devices — wheeled AMRs, quadrupeds and humanoids — on an open stack (ROS 2, Open-RMF, Zenoh, EdgeX). On the roadmap, the same Forge-to-edge loop will feed vision-language-action (VLA) and physical-AI models to these robots: perception models trained in Forge, deployed over Horizon, and closed through Fleet and Link.

docs.title: Product suite
docs.text:
Two thin suite services tie the family together; six domain products do the work. Every domain product is a complete system that can run on its own. Short names are used in prose and abbreviations in diagrams — see Naming & abbreviations.

Product Abbr. What it does NereidSphere NS Thin suite layer — single portal, unified API gateway, and cross-product event glue. NereidIdentity NI Suite SSO and identity center — OIDC / LDAP / SAML federation, RBAC, token issuance. NereidLink NL Privatized IoT data pipeline — device access, rule engine, alerting, dashboards. NereidForge NF Model factory — datasets, training, optimization, multi-silicon export, registry. NereidHorizon NH Edge distribution — policy-driven rollout, bandwidth-aware delivery, OTA. NereidEdge NE Southbound edge integration on field gateways — zero-touch, mTLS, autonomy. NereidFleet NFL Robot fleet management — task scheduling, traffic control, teleoperation. NereidMobile NM Operator's window into Link — mobile app and WeChat Mini Program.

docs.title: The name
docs.text: "Nereid" is simply the mascot name we chose — it carries no hidden or particularly deep meaning. In Greek mythology, the Nereids are the spirits of the sea (海之精灵), daughters of Nereus. We liked the image, so we made it the project's mascot and the shared prefix for every product.

docs.title: What the mascot stands for
docs.text:
Picture a spirit swimming through an ocean of data:

  • navigating the sea of data — finding a path through the devices, models, and pipelines of an AIoT system;
  • helping users find their way — turning a fragmented edge-to-cloud stack into one clear, closed loop;
  • spotting the hidden reefs — vendor lock-in, mandatory cloud dependence, data leaving the customer perimeter, and models that never make it to the field.

The reefs are exactly what the platform is designed to steer around.

docs.title: Our mission
docs.text:
Democratize AIoT by integrating edge and cloud workflows into one seamless closed loop — low-latency edge inference, privacy-preserving operations, and automated model monitoring, all in a single platform.

In practice that means a small team can keep turning its own business data into models that run on its own field devices: data never has to leave the customer's perimeter, there is no mandatory cloud, and no single silicon or edge vendor is baked into the platform.

docs.title: How the family is named
docs.text:
Every product shares the Nereid prefix; the suffix says what it does:

Name The suffix suggests NereidSphere the sphere that holds the suite together — portal, gateway, glue NereidIdentity identity and access NereidLink linking devices into the platform NereidForge the forge where models are made NereidHorizon reaching the distant horizon of remote edge nodes NereidEdge the edge, on field gateways NereidFleet a fleet of robots NereidMobile the mobile window

The commercial industry solutions follow the same spirit — NereidFactory, NereidSentinel, NereidMedical. See Naming & abbreviations.

docs.title: What we believe
docs.text:
• Private by design — fully air-gapped operation, no mandatory call-home.
  • Open source, commercially supported — Apache-2.0 community edition; enterprise LTS and turnkey delivery under commercial terms.
  • Loosely coupled products — every product stands alone; the suite layer only federates them. See Standalone by default.
  • Vendor-neutral contracts — no hard dependency on one edge stack or one silicon vendor.

docs.title: Cross-Product Contracts
docs.text: Products are autonomous, so the only things that bind the suite are explicit contracts. These are kept small, versioned, and vendor-neutral; a change to one is a suite-level event, not a local refactor.

docs.title: The contracts
docs.text:
Contract Parties What it fixes Gateway wire protocol v1 Link ↔ Edge Topics, frames, and catalogs for the southbound gateway link (v1/gateway/*): telemetry, attributes, shadow, commands, discovery, OTA. Implemented; frozen before a release candidate. SSO / OIDC federation Sphere ↔ Identity ↔ products How a browser session becomes a product session: either ticket handoff or a direct OIDC client. See SSO & OIDC. Read-only mobile API subset Mobile ↔ Link The narrow read surface a mobile client needs: auth, devices, telemetry, alerts. Artifact hand-off Forge → Horizon How produced model / application packages become rollout-ready artifacts. Edge distribution channel Horizon → Edge How Edge itself, apps, and models are delivered and updated. The edge OTA channel is owned by Horizon, not by Edge.

Contract status

Contracts are finalized before a release candidate; anything not contract-ready is moved out of the release rather than shipped half-defined. Individual statuses are tracked in the suite development plan.

docs.title: Contract rules
docs.text:
These apply to every contract above and to each product's public API:

  • OpenAPI is the spec. APIs are described with OpenAPI 3.1, and the spec moves in the same change as the code. Specs are validated (they must parse) as part of the contract; Sphere and Link both ship an embedded, offline Swagger UI so an air-gapped operator can read the contract without a CDN.
  • Empty arrays are [], never null. Clients may rely on the shape.
  • No invented semantics. The platform never guesses meaning — e.g. units come only from user-defined descriptors.
  • Neutral by construction. Contracts stay protocol-, stack-, and vendor-agnostic. No generic interface hard-depends on a specific edge stack or silicon vendor; vendor specifics stay inside Forge.
  • Migrations are explicit and reversible. Schema changes ship as numbered, paired up/down migrations — never auto-mutated at startup.
  • i18n moves together. No hardcoded user-facing strings; new keys land in both locales in the same change.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
Each product is an independent repository under the NereidAI organization; a contract change touches the contract document and every affected implementation in one coordinated change.

  • Product suite overview
  • Architecture overview

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
NereidAI is a suite of independently deployable products that together form one edge-to-cloud loop. There is no single monolith: the suite layer federates the products, and each domain product owns its own data, APIs, and release cycle.

  • Suite layer (thin): Sphere (portal, unified API gateway, event glue) and Identity (SSO, RBAC).
  • Domain products: Link (IoT pipeline), Forge (model factory), Horizon (edge distribution).
  • Edge / field: Edge (southbound integration on field gateways), Fleet (robot fleets), and the field devices themselves.
  • Thin clients: Mobile.

docs.title: The closed loop
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph FIELD["Site / field"]
        DEV["devices · sensors · cameras"]
        EDGE["NE\nfield gateway"]
    end
    subgraph CENTER["Private platform (cloud / central DC)"]
        LINK["NL\ningest · rules · alerts"]
        FORGE["NF\nmodel factory"]
        HORIZON["NH\nedge distribution"]
    end
    CV["computer vision /\ndata consumers"]

    DEV -->|southbound| EDGE
    EDGE -->|mTLS · store-and-forward| LINK
    LINK -->|datasets| FORGE
    FORGE -->|models / apps| HORIZON
    HORIZON -->|policy rollout · OTA| EDGE
    LINK -->|telemetry · events| CV

The loop is deliberate: field data flows in, becomes training data, becomes models, is distributed back out to the field, and the resulting telemetry feeds the next iteration — with no mandatory cloud dependency at any hop.

docs.title: Communication planes
docs.text: Plane How it works Device / southbound Edge is an EdgeX Foundry application service that bridges field devices to Link over the gateway MQTT protocol (v1/gateway/*). Transport is TLS/mTLS; buffering is store-and-forward so intermittent WAN links do not lose data. Ingest Link accepts MQTT, HTTP, and CoAP through one shared envelope and SDK, so behaviour is identical across transports. Ingress is rate-limited per device token. Service-to-service (Link) Services communicate only over NATS — never by direct cross-service database access. Realtime to clients All live data (telemetry, presence, alarms, command progress, OTA progress…) is pushed over a single WebSocket connection with multi-subscription; REST is used only for snapshots and writes. Polling is deliberately avoided. Management / SSO Browsers reach products through Sphere, which authenticates against Identity (OIDC) and hands identity to products via a sealed ticket. See SSO & OIDC.

docs.title: Suite integration
docs.text: In the default suite deployment, products do not each implement their own login. The browser signs in once against Identity (through Sphere); Sphere then issues a short-lived, single-use sealed ticket that the product backend exchanges server-to-server for the verified identity. Identity is the single source of truth for identities (Keycloak realm nereidai); Sphere never stores users. Products can also run fully standalone, either with a direct OIDC client or with local accounts.

docs.title: Technology stack
docs.text: Product Stack (confirmed) Sphere Go 1.24, stdlib net/http, log/slog, cobra; React 18 + Ant Design 5 + Vite + TypeScript, embedded into the binary; OIDC relying party; Valkey for multi-replica ticket replay HA Identity Keycloak 26 + dedicated PostgreSQL (replaceable OIDC engine), declaratively provisioned realm/clients Link Go, gRPC, NATS (Core / JetStream / KV), PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB, S3-compatible object storage; MQTT / HTTP / CoAP ingress; WebSocket push Forge FastAPI (Python) backend + worker, React + TS + Ant Design + Vite frontend, Kubeflow Pipelines, Helm charts; images from the private registry Horizon React 18 / Vite frontend + Express BFF, PostgreSQL; drives Open Horizon Exchange / agbot / edge nodes Edge Go (EdgeX Foundry App Functions SDK v4), runs on field gateways Fleet See the product page — early stage (Tech Preview) Mobile Mobile app and WeChat Mini Program served from a single client codebase

docs.title: Design invariants
docs.text:
• Private by design — fully air-gapped operation, no mandatory call-home, no runtime internet dependency.
  • Product autonomy — each product owns its domain end to end; the suite layer never absorbs domain logic.
  • Neutral contracts — APIs and wire contracts stay protocol-, stack-, and vendor-agnostic; no hard dependency on a particular edge stack or silicon vendor in generic interfaces.
  • Multi-silicon via the factory — vendor-specific toolchains live only inside Forge; every other product consumes versioned artifacts.

See also: Topology and Cross-Product Contracts.

docs.title: Deployment Topology
docs.text: A NereidAI installation spans two physical tiers joined by an often-intermittent WAN: a private platform (cloud or central data center), and one or more sites / fields where devices actually live. Everything is designed to keep running when the WAN link is degraded or down.

    end

        direction TB
        EDGEG["NE\nfield gateway (EdgeX)"]
        FLEETC["NFL\nrobot control loop"]
        DEVICES["devices · sensors · cameras"]

    end

    SPHERE --> LINKC
    SPHERE --> FORGEC
    SPHERE --> HORIZONC
    ID <--> SPHERE
    MOB -->|telemetry · charts · alerts| LINKC
    EDGEG -->|telemetry · mTLS · store-and-forward| LINKC
    HORIZONC -->|OTA: NE + apps / models| EDGEG

    INFRA --- LINKC

docs.title: Central platform
docs.text:
The central tier runs on Kubernetes (k3s or a full cluster) via Helm charts, or — for Link — as a single all-in-one binary. Which products you run is your choice; each is independently installable, and none requires the others to start.

Component Role Sphere Portal and unified API gateway; reverse proxy to products; SSO glue Identity Keycloak realm nereidai; the identity source of truth Link Device ingest, message backbone, rules, alerts, dashboards, OTA orchestration Forge Dataset / annotation, training, optimization, multi-silicon export, registry (Kubeflow Pipelines) Horizon Policy-driven distribution of Edge, apps, and models to remote nodes Mobile Read-only operator window: telemetry, charts, alerts

docs.title: Shared infrastructure
docs.text:
Dependency Used by Notes PostgreSQL most products Link uses PostgreSQL + TimescaleDB for entity and time-series data NATS Link Core / JetStream / KV; the only path for service-to-service communication S3-compatible object storage Link, Forge e.g. SeaweedFS; firmware packages, datasets, cold data Private image registry all e.g. Harbor; no internet dependency at runtime Kubeflow Pipelines Forge training / optimization / evaluation pipelines Open Horizon Horizon Exchange / agbot / edge nodes for large-scale rollout

Air-gapped profile

In an air-gapped install, all images come from an internal mirror / private registry and the whole platform is delivered as an offline bundle. See Air-Gapped Install.

docs.title: Site / field tier
docs.text:
• Edge runs on a field gateway and bridges southbound devices (through EdgeX device services) into Link. It holds a store-and-forward buffer so that telemetry survives WAN outages, and it is delivered / updated by Horizon over the same WAN.
  • Fleet runs the low-latency local control loop for robot fleets (commands / state stay on the LAN), while fleet management reaches it over the management plane.
  • Devices connect either directly to Link (MQTT / HTTP / CoAP) or through a Edge gateway.

docs.title: Network characteristics
docs.text: Link Behaviour Device → Edge local, southbound, via EdgeX device services Edge → Link TLS / mTLS over WAN, store-and-forward, replay-safe Horizon → Edge policy-driven rollout, bandwidth-aware, offline reconciliation Browser → Sphere → products SSO over the management plane (WAN) Fleet ↔ robots real-time, low-latency LAN

docs.title: Community vs Enterprise
docs.text:
The community edition covers the complete edge-to-cloud loop and can be used in production on its own. Enterprise capabilities cover the procurement, operations, and compliance needs of large organizations.

The table below reproduces the capability comparison from the NereidAI project overview.

Capability Community Enterprise value Edge connectors & NPU adapter plugins ✓ Same capabilities, with vendor-backed integration support Link / Forge / Horizon, single-site ✓ Multi-site scale — federated operation across many sites, certified hardware/accelerator combinations, and vendor-supported rollout with LTS Sphere + Identity multi-tenant control plane — Unified identity and cross-product governance — one login, one portal, consistent tenants and policies across the suite Identity external IdP federation (OIDC / LDAP / SAML) and SCIM provisioning — Enterprise IAM integration — connect to an existing directory and automate user lifecycle management High availability, disaster recovery, large-scale rollout policy — Scale and resilience — fleet-wide rollouts with HA/DR for sites that cannot tolerate downtime Audit, hardening, compliance baselines (等保 / MLPS etc.) — Compliance and audit readiness for regulated industries and SOE / multinational procurement Signed release artifacts and per-release SBOM ✓ Plus signed offline bundles and enterprise supply-chain workflows CVE response SLA and backported fixes — Contractual response commitment with fixes backported to LTS versions Air-gapped delivery, private POC, training self-service Turnkey delivery and knowledge transfer on the customer's premises Support GitHub issues / Discussions (community only, no SLA) 7×24 LTS with a named engineer

docs.title: How to read this table
docs.text:
• A ✓ in the Community column means the capability is available in the Apache-2.0 community edition; a — means it is a commercial capability.
  • "Community" is not a crippled edition. The community edition is a complete, production-usable edge-to-cloud loop. Enterprise value is about scale, governance, and assurance — running many sites, meeting procurement and audit requirements, and getting contractual commitments.
  • The self-service entry for air-gapped delivery means the community edition supports it, while commercial terms add turnkey delivery and knowledge transfer.

docs.title: Security & delivery posture
docs.text:
The same posture work that underpins the community edition also determines what is planned or commercial. From the project overview:

Capability Status Air-gapped / offline installation (full image bundles, no internet required) Available No mandatory call-home; data stays inside the customer perimeter Available mTLS service-to-service and device-to-platform links Available Unified SSO and centralized RBAC across all suite products (Identity) Available Signed release artifacts and per-release SBOM Planned Enterprise SLA on CVE response and backported fixes Commercial contract Compliance baselines (e.g. 等保 2.0) and local-OS / accelerator certifications Per-engagement roadmap

docs.text:

  • Modify it and distribute your modifications.
  • Combine it with your own code without a copyleft obligation on that code.

docs.text:

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
This page summarizes the v0.0.1 suite release plan. It is a living plan: dates are not fixed — phases are entered and exited by gate criteria, not by the calendar. The plan reflected here was last updated 2026-10-11.

Status is tracked in the open

This page describes the plan as of 2026-10-11. Current status is tracked in the NereidAI GitHub organization and in Discussions.

docs.title: v0.0.1 in one paragraph
docs.text: v0.0.1 is the first installable snapshot of the edge-to-cloud loop published under the NereidAI suite. Each repository keeps its own VERSION (v0.0.1 until GA; build identity v0.0.1+git<sha>.<date>). This page tracks the suite-level view.

docs.title: Maturity gates
docs.text:
Each product ships at one of three maturity gates:

Gate Meaning Criteria GA Production-ready Air-gapped install verified; API frozen; load/burn-in targets met; docs complete; signed images + SBOM Preview Tryable, not stable Core flows work end to end; installable; contracts may still change; partial docs Tech Preview Demoable minimal loop Smallest end-to-end slice; no upgrade or API stability promise

docs.title: Where each product stands
docs.text:
Baseline state as of 2026-10-11:

Product Gate Baseline state Link GA Feature-complete single binary; its own GA plan exists (docs/roadmap/ga.md). Edge GA Core bridge and connector governance done; E2E acceptance pending. Forge Preview Functionally mature (dataset / train / optimize / export / registry); no GA plan yet. Horizon Preview Web UI and BFF under development; MVP scope to be frozen. Sphere Tech Preview Empty repository; built from zero. Mobile Tech Preview Repository not created; built from zero. Fleet Tech Preview Research docs only; no commits.

Be honest: some products are Tech Preview

Sphere, Mobile, and Fleet are at Tech Preview — a demoable minimal loop with no upgrade or API stability promise. Forge and Horizon are at Preview, so their contracts may still change. Only Link and Edge are at GA.

docs.title: The five phases
docs.text:
Exit each phase only when its gate is met; reordering within a phase is allowed.

  1. Foundation — Repos, CI, and scaffolding for new products. Link and Edge close their P0/P1 items. Forge and Horizon freeze v0.0.1 scope. Mobile Taro proof-of-concept. Fleet MVP converged from research.
  2. Build — Main user flows in every product. All cross-product contracts are finalized by the end of this phase.
  3. Integration — Cross-product end-to-end testing; Link/Edge wire-contract freeze; load and fault-injection tests for GA products.
  4. Release candidate — Multi-arch images, SBOM, vulnerability scan, signatures, signed offline bundles, full air-gapped install rehearsal, burn-in, docs pass.
  5. Release — Per-repository GitHub releases; the suite guide goes live with links and status badges/levels.

Anything not contract-ready by the end of Build, or not stable by RC, is moved out of v0.0.1 rather than delaying the phase.

Cross-product contracts (summary)

Contracts must be finalized by the end of the Build phase.

Contract Parties Status Gateway wire protocol v1 (topics, frames, catalogs) Link ↔ Edge Implemented; freezes before RC SSO / OIDC federation Sphere ↔ Keycloak ↔ products Not started; Sphere integrates Keycloak directly first Read-only mobile API subset (auth, devices, telemetry, alerts) Mobile ↔ Link Not defined Artifact hand-off (model/app packages → rollout) Forge → Horizon Not defined Edge distribution channel Horizon → Edge Horizon is the owner

No other contact channel is published on this site.

What community support is not

Community support does not include contractual response times, private engineering time, deployment on your premises, or backported fixes to older releases. Those are commercial capabilities — see Community vs Enterprise.

docs.title: Air-Gapped Installation
docs.text:
NereidAI is designed for sovereign, regulated, and network-isolated environments. Every product supports fully air-gapped operation: there is no internet dependency at runtime and no mandatory call-home. A privatized installation pulls only from internal mirrors and a private registry, and every byte stays inside the customer perimeter.

Scope

This page explains how offline delivery works and what it guarantees. For Kubernetes topologies see Kubernetes & Helm; for how updates reach the field see Edge Delivery.

docs.title: The offline guarantee
docs.text:
The suite-wide security posture is the contract this approach implements:

Capability Status Air-gapped / offline installation (full image bundles, no internet required) Available No mandatory call-home; data stays inside the customer perimeter Available mTLS service-to-service and device-to-platform links Available Unified SSO and centralized RBAC across all products (Identity) Available Signed release artifacts and per-release SBOM Planned Enterprise SLA on CVE response and backported fixes Commercial contract Compliance baselines (e.g. 等保 2.0) and local-OS / accelerator certifications Per-engagement roadmap

Two invariants make this work:

  • Nothing may introduce a runtime external dependency. Privatized builds pull only from internal mirrors and the private registry.
  • The platform never phones home. Telemetry, models, and identity stay inside the deployment.

docs.title: What an offline bundle contains
docs.text:
An offline delivery (a full image bundle) is self-contained. It carries, at minimum:

  • Container images for the suite and its dependencies, mirrored from a vendor build host — the identity engine, databases, message backbone, and each product.
  • Helm charts for the product releases and their dependencies.
  • An image manifest recording exactly which images and tags were mirrored, so the isolated side can be verified against it.

Two repositories, both internal

Images live in a private registry (Harbor in the reference deployment); charts are served from an internal chart repository. In the isolated environment both are reached over the intranet only.

docs.title: How an offline installation proceeds
docs.text:
The shape is the same for every product — mirror, transfer, import, install, verify — even though each product ships its own offline-preparation tooling:

flowchart LR
    BUILD["Connected build host\nmirror images + charts"]
    BUNDLE["Offline bundle\n(media / transfer)"]
    IMPORT["Isolated deploy host\npush into private registry"]
    NODES["Nodes pull\nvia internal mirror"]

    BUILD --> BUNDLE --> IMPORT --> NODES
  1. Prepare on a connected build host. Mirror every image the release needs into the bundle and record a manifest. Each product provides scripts that mirror images and package them (Forge also groups images into categories).
  2. Transfer the bundle to the isolated environment over whatever out-of-band channel the site allows (removable media, a one-way transfer host).
  3. Import into the private registry and confirm every image resolves from the registry rather than a public source.
  4. Point the nodes at the internal mirror so the container runtime resolves pulls to the private registry — applied identically to every node.
  5. Install from the internal chart repository using the normal Helm flow described in Kubernetes & Helm.
  6. Verify. Run the product's verification step: everything must pull from the private registry, with no public-registry references left in the rendered manifests.

Reuse before rebuild

Imported images are used as-is; the isolated side does not build from source or install packages at runtime — the images already contain their dependencies.

docs.title: Why identity and storage are in the bundle
docs.text:
The offline bundle must include the pieces every product assumes:

  • Identity (the identity engine plus its dedicated database) is the suite identity source of truth; it is deployed once and shared. See SSO & OIDC.
  • Stateful dependencies — the time-series database, the message backbone, and optional S3-compatible object storage — travel with the bundle, so a site with no object store can still run the pipeline.

docs.title: Supply chain
docs.text:
• Signed release artifacts and a per-release SBOM are on the roadmap (listed as planned in the security posture); signed offline bundles and enterprise supply-chain workflows are offered under commercial terms.
  • Containers are tracked by manifest digest; mirrored images keep their digests through the import.

Operations documentation

Step-by-step installation and operations detail lives in each product repository: github.com/NereidAI.

docs.title: Edge Delivery
docs.text:
Horizon is the edge distribution and deployment product. It distributes Edge itself, plus applications and models, to large numbers of remote edge nodes: policy-driven rollout, bandwidth-aware delivery, OTA lifecycle, and autonomous reconciliation while offline.

The nodes it targets are field gateways running Edge, the southbound integration layer that connects field devices into Link.

docs.title: The distribution loop
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    FORGE["NF\nmodels / apps"]
    HORIZON["NH\npolicy rollout · OTA"]
    EDGE["NE\nfield gateway"]
    DEV["devices · sensors · cameras"]
    LINK["NL\ningest · rules · alerts"]

    FORGE -->|versioned artifacts| HORIZON
    HORIZON -->|agreements · OTA lifecycle| EDGE
    EDGE -->|cmds / data| DEV
    DEV -->|telemetry| EDGE
    EDGE -->|mTLS · store-and-forward| LINK

Forge produces models and applications; Horizon delivers them (and Edge itself) to the field; Edge runs them on the gateway and bridges the field devices; and device telemetry flows back to Link — the same loop described in the architecture overview.

docs.title: Policy-driven rollout
docs.text:
Horizon builds on Open Horizon: its console drives the Exchange and the agreement bots that deploy workloads to edge nodes. Rollout is expressed as policy and patterns, not per-device scripts:

  • Services are the deployable units, governed by policies, patterns, and management policies that decide where they run.
  • Nodes are the field targets; agreement bots form and maintain the agreements that keep the intended services running.
  • Rollouts are phased and canary-based — percentage or fixed-size batches that advance only after an observation pause, with circuit breakers that abort a rollout automatically on failure thresholds.

Service deployments are signed before they are published, and the matching public key is uploaded alongside the service — an integrity check on the distribution path.

docs.title: Bandwidth-aware delivery
docs.text:
Field links are frequently intermittent and low-bandwidth, so delivery is designed to survive them:

  • Store-and-forward at the edge means a link outage does not lose data; the gateway buffers and forwards when the link returns.
  • Resumable downloads let a large artifact survive a partial transfer rather than restart; download progress is streamed to the UI but not stored as telemetry.
  • Autonomous reconciliation while offline: the edge keeps operating on its last known-good configuration and reconciles with the platform on reconnect.

docs.title: The OTA lifecycle
docs.text:
Edge is delivered and kept up to date by Horizon over an OTA lifecycle. Two sources are supported: an external URL (the edge downloads it itself, with enforced integrity verification) or platform-hosted packages in object storage behind an authenticated path (so edges need no object-store credentials).

Updates move through staged phases — pending, downloading, verified, updating, rebooting, confirmed — with structured result codes for precise diagnosis. Process control includes pause, resume, and tiered cancellation: not-yet-started targets stop immediately while in-progress updates are not interrupted and their results are still collected.

docs.title: NereidEdge on the field gateway
docs.text:
Edge runs on field gateways as an EdgeX Foundry application service. It provides:

  • Zero-touch onboarding — devices auto-connect on first telemetry, and the edge periodically reports a manifest of its attached device list.
  • Secure mTLS links to Link, with an outbound-only connection to the Link gateway.
  • Local autonomy — manifest reconciliation, heartbeat liveness grading, and connector desired-state reconciliation continue without the platform.
  • Handshake negotiation and feature gating — on connect the edge negotiates protocol version and feature set; non-overlapping versions or missing required features are rejected.
  • Configuration lifecycle — the platform pushes desired state and the edge reports actual state, with two levels of configuration (profile templates plus instance overrides) merged at dispatch.
  • Schema validation and drift reconciliation — edges advertise connector config schemas, and periodic list reconciliation identifies missing, stale, drifted, and extra instances.

The edge stays reachable on its own LAN

Edge connects to Link over the WAN with an outbound mTLS link; site-local commands and state (for example Fleet ↔ robots) run over the low-latency local LAN and do not depend on the central link.

docs.title: Kubernetes & Helm
docs.text: Every domain product is a complete system that can run on its own, and every one of them can run on Kubernetes. The suite layer does not deploy the products for you — each product owns its own namespace, Helm release, and release lifecycle.

docs.title: One codebase, two forms
docs.text:
Link is the clearest example of the delivery duality: one codebase, two forms.

Form Where Dependencies Single host (all-in-one) A single static binary plus a local stack Bundles its own database, message backbone, and optional object storage Kubernetes / K3s The product's Helm chart Bundled database and message backbone; object storage reused or bring-your-own

The same product binary serves both forms. The minimum stateful dependencies are only a database and a message backbone; object storage is optional (needed for platform-hosted firmware uploads, not for external-URL OTA).

docs.title: Namespaces and topology
docs.text:
In the reference topology each product lives in its own namespace, named after the product itself, and the identity plane is deployed once for the whole suite:

flowchart TB
    subgraph CENTER["Central management cluster"]
        ID["nereididentity\nidentity engine"]
        SPHERE["nereidsphere\nportal · OIDC RP · ticket hub"]
        HORIZON["nereidhorizon\nedge distribution"]
        FORGE["nereidforge\nmodel factory"]
    end
    subgraph CONN["Connection plane (scale out horizontally)"]
        LINK["nereidlink\nMQTT ingress · ingest · rules"]
    end
    SPHERE -->|ticket / OIDC| LINK
    SPHERE -->|ticket / OIDC| HORIZON
    ID -.->|issuer| SPHERE
    LINK -->|mTLS| EDGE["NE\nfield gateways"]
  • Identity is a single suite-wide plane. No matter how many connection-plane clusters exist, they authenticate against one issuer rather than each running an identity service.
  • The connection plane scales by adding clusters, not by adding namespaces: isolate MQTT ingress, ingest, and time-series load per tenant or device range.
  • Multi-tenancy is a product concept, not a namespace boundary. Tenants live inside the product's business model; a Kubernetes namespace is not a tenant.

In production each product namespace carries its own resource quotas, a default-deny network policy with explicit allowances, and an independent registry pull secret. A lab/POC install can instead use a single all-in-one namespace.

docs.title: Helm charts and versioning
docs.text:
Charts come from the internal chart repository. All the derived versions — the chart version, its appVersion, and the image tag — come from a single VERSION source of truth, so they cannot drift: the chart version drops the leading v while the app version and image tag keep it. An empty image tag falls back to the chart's app version.

Deploy the identity plane first, then the portal, then the products: the portal is the suite's only OIDC relying party and must be reachable before products can verify handoffs.

docs.title: NereidSphere deployment behaviour
docs.text:
Sphere is a stateless portal with sealed cookie sessions, and its chart exposes the choices that matter at install time:

  • Authentication mode. By default Sphere authenticates against the identity engine. An emergency local mode with bcrypt accounts declared at deploy time exists for disaster recovery when the identity plane is unreachable — it is break-glass only, never the production default. See SSO & OIDC.
  • Multi-replica ticket safety. A handoff ticket is single-use. With more than one Sphere replica the single-use claim must be shared, so Sphere uses a Valkey key-value topology for cross-replica enforcement. If it cannot confirm single use it fails closed rather than risk a replay; a process-memory store is limited to single-replica development and the chart refuses to render multiple replicas with it.

docs.title: High availability and bring-your-own infrastructure
docs.text:
• Link HA ships as an opt-in overlay: multiple app pods, a CloudNativePG PostgreSQL, a multi-node NATS JetStream, shared read-write-many storage, and NATS-KV leader election. The default stays single-node.
  • Bring-your-own infrastructure is supported by disabling the bundled dependencies and supplying endpoints and credentials for an existing database, message backbone, and object store. The chart fails fast if an external dependency is selected but its endpoint is left empty.

docs.title: Private registry
docs.text:
All deployment images come from the private registry (Harbor in the reference deployment); there are no public-registry pulls at deploy time. A registry pull secret is carried into each namespace, and a node-level mirror configuration lets the container runtime resolve the registry on air-gapped clusters (see Air-Gapped Install).

docs.title: Platform Integration
docs.text:
This guide is for backend systems and third-party developers that call the NereidAI platform programmatically. Every product ships its own complete OpenAPI contract; this page does not repeat those endpoints. It answers the two questions that decide an integration: which product's API do I call, and how do I authenticate — then points to the exact spec.

Upper-layer documentation

This is a capability-and-flow guide for integrators. Per-endpoint request and response schemas live in each product's OpenAPI document, and deep developer documentation lives in the product repositories — see NereidAI.

docs.title: Choose your entry point
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[Your system] --> Q{What are you integrating?}
    Q -->|Device / gateway firmware| D[NL southbound protocol<br/>MQTT or HTTP device endpoints]
    Q -->|Backend service, no interactive user| M{Which data?}
    Q -->|Browser user inside the suite| S[NS single sign-on<br/>then call via the gateway]
    Q -->|One product without the suite| O[Direct OIDC client against NI]
    M -->|Devices, telemetry, remote control| ML[NL REST API<br/>OAuth2 client_credentials]
    M -->|Edge nodes, services, agreements| MH[NH Partner API<br/>X-Api-Key, read-only]
    S --> GW[/NS gateway /p/{product}/]
You are… Use Authentication A sensor, controller or edge gateway reporting data / taking commands NL southbound (v1/me/* over MQTT/HTTP) Device credential (token / id+secret / X.509) A server application reading devices/telemetry or issuing commands NL platform REST (/v1/tenants/...) OAuth2 client_credentials → Bearer JWT A third-party system reading edge exchange inventory NH Partner API (/api/v1/{org}/...) Partner API key (X-Api-Key) A web application used by signed-in suite users Product APIs through the NS gateway Suite session cookie; CSRF on writes A product integrated without the suite portal The product's own OIDC login Authorization-code + PKCE against NI

The four authentication flows with full sequence diagrams are on the next page: Authentication Flows.

docs.title: API catalog
docs.text:
Every product is independently deployable and has its own origin. The suite portal is only involved when Sphere is the entry point.

Product API surface Typical base path Machine auth Contract NS (Sphere) Portal, SSO ticket hub, gateway, admin /auth/*, /api/v1/*, /p/{product}/* X-NS-Client-Id + X-NS-Client-Secret for server-to-server calls Embedded OpenAPI + offline Swagger UI at /api/docs NL (Link) Platform REST: tenants, devices, profiles, telemetry, OTA, commands /v1/tenants/{tenantId}/... OAuth2 POST /v1/auth/token (client_credentials) → Bearer JWT Embedded Swagger UI at /api/docs NL device ingress Device/gateway wire protocol MQTT topics v1/me/*, v1/gateway/*; HTTP /v1/me/* Device credential Same OpenAPI (device tags) + Device SDK NF (Forge) Model factory console API (datasets, training jobs, models) /api/v1/... Session-oriented (suite ticket or local JWT login); tenant from X-Tenant-Id docs/api/openapi.yaml NH (Horizon) console Management console API /api/... Suite session cookie + CSRF openapi-console.yaml NH partner Read-only edge exchange proxy for third parties /api/v1/{org}/... X-Api-Key (nk_live_… / nk_test_…) openapi-partner.yaml NI (Identity) Standard OIDC / OAuth2 (Keycloak-compatible realm nereidai) /auth/realms/nereidai/protocol/openid-connect/* Client credentials per registered client OIDC discovery document NE (Edge) No independent REST API — Acts as an NL gateway over the southbound wire protocol See Gateway integration NFL / NM (Fleet / Mobile) No public OpenAPI in this release — Fleet is Tech Preview; Mobile uses the narrow Link mobile API subset Product repositories

Products are independent

You can buy/deploy NL alone, NH alone, and so on. Suite SSO and the /p/ gateway exist only in a suite deployment where NS is the entry point; a standalone product is reached directly at its own origin and authenticates per its own contract.

docs.title: The identity plane
docs.text:
• NI (Identity) is the only identity source of truth. Its issuer is a Keycloak-compatible realm, for example https://sso.yiqisoft.cn/auth/realms/nereidai (development: http://localhost:8090/realms/nereidai).
  • Standard OIDC endpoints are published under the issuer's /.well-known/openid-configuration (authorization, token, JWKS, userinfo).
  • In a suite deployment NS is the only component that speaks OIDC to NI. Backend integrations normally never touch NI directly: machines get NL service-account tokens, browsers sign in at NS.
  • Customer identity systems (Entra ID, Okta, AD FS, …) are brokered behind NI; they never change the API contracts. See SSO & OIDC for the identity model.

docs.title: Calling conventions
docs.text: These rules apply across products; per-endpoint details are in each OpenAPI document.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
• All REST traffic is JSON over HTTPS (Content-Type: application/json), UTF-8. Device media upload is the documented binary exception (POST /v1/me/blob).
  • Authenticate with an Authorization: Bearer <jwt> header (NL REST), X-Api-Key (NH partner), or the suite session cookie when calling through the NS gateway. Never invent identity headers (X-User-*, X-NS-Integration-Secret) — inbound copies are stripped; only the gateway may set them.
  • Scope every call to your tenant/org. NL encodes it in the path (/v1/tenants/{tenantId}/...); NF reads it from the token or X-Tenant-Id; an NH partner key is bound to exactly one org and any other org returns 403.
  • Send or honor X-Request-Id for correlation. If you do not provide one, the gateway generates it; echoing it in your logs makes support traceable.

docs.title: Responses
docs.text:
• Success and error bodies are JSON. Arrays are always [], never null.
  • Use the standard status codes: 401 (missing/expired credential — get a new token), 403 (authenticated but not assigned/authorized), 404, 409 (conflict), 413/415 (media size/type), 429 (rate limited — NL also temporarily locks an OAuth client after repeated failed logins), 503 (for example NL blob storage not configured).
  • Machine tokens are short-lived (NL: expires_in, typically 1800 s) and have no refresh token — re-run the client-credentials exchange before/on expiry.
  • The platform never invents semantics such as measurement units; they come from user-defined descriptors. See cross-product contracts.

docs.title: Air-gapped operation
docs.text: All endpoints, Swagger UIs and base models are served on-premises with no CDN or cloud dependency. Partner keys, service-account secrets and OIDC clients are provisioned by the operator; integrate against the internal origins published for your deployment.

docs.title: Typical recipes
docs.text: The end-to-end sequences — token call, suite user, partner key, device media — are on Authentication Flows, each with a runnable request example.

docs.title: Related
docs.text:
• Authentication Flows — the four flows, step by step.
  • SSO & OIDC · RBAC — the identity and authorization model.
  • Device SDK (Go) · Binary media and S3 — device-side integration.
  • Cross-product contracts — compatibility rules.

docs.title: Authentication Flows
docs.text:
This page walks each integration flow end to end. Pick the flow that matches your caller type from Platform Integration; the sequence diagram shows who talks to whom, and the recipe is a runnable request.

Flow Caller Credential Interactive user? A Backend service → NL REST OAuth2 client_credentials Bearer JWT No B Backend / third party → NH edge data Partner API key No C Browser user → any product in a suite NS session + gateway / ticket Yes D Device or gateway firmware Device credential over MQTT/HTTP No E A product deployed without the suite OIDC authorization-code + PKCE Yes

Identity concepts (why there is one identity plane, where customer IdPs plug in) are on SSO & OIDC.

docs.title: Flow A — backend service calling NL (client_credentials)
docs.text:
Use this for servers that read devices/telemetry or issue commands with no interactive user. The operator creates a service account in NL scoped to a tenant with chosen scopes; you receive a client_id and client_secret.

sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Your backend
    participant NL as NereidLink
    App->>NL: POST /v1/auth/token (client_id + client_secret)
    NL-->>App: access_token (JWT, expires_in ~1800s)
    App->>NL: GET /v1/tenants/{tenant}/devices<br/>Authorization: Bearer <token>
    NL-->>App: 200 JSON
    Note over App,NL: On 401: re-run the token exchange (no refresh token)

The token endpoint accepts the credentials as JSON, as a form body, or as HTTP Basic auth; only grant_type=client_credentials is supported.

# 1) Exchange the service-account credentials for a machine token
TOKEN=$(curl -sS https://link.example/v1/auth/token \
  -u "$NL_CLIENT_ID:$NL_CLIENT_SECRET" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"grant_type":"client_credentials"}' | jq -r .access_token)

# 2) Call a tenant-scoped REST endpoint
curl -sS "https://link.example/v1/tenants/$TENANT_ID/devices?page=1&page_size=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Token response: {"access_token":"…","token_type":"Bearer","expires_in":1800}.

  • Cache the token until shortly before expires_in; there is deliberately no refresh token — present the secret again.
  • Repeated failed logins for one client id are temporarily locked with 429 regardless of source address; treat secrets as configuration, never log them.
  • The same JWT is the BearerAuth scheme documented in the OpenAPI document.
  • Command/control endpoints require the corresponding service-account scope; read-only integrations should be granted read scopes only.

docs.title: Flow B — third party reading edge data from NH (partner key)
docs.text:
For an external system that only needs to read Open Horizon exchange resources (services, patterns, policies, nodes, agreements, users, HA groups). The operator issues a partner key in the console; the key is bound to one organization.

sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Partner system
    participant NH as NereidHorizon BFF
    participant EX as Edge Exchange
    P->>NH: GET /api/v1/{org}/nodes<br/>X-Api-Key: nk_live_…
    NH->>NH: key valid? org matches? GET only?
    NH->>EX: proxy with the shared exchange credential
    EX-->>NH: exchange response
    NH-->>P: 200 JSON (call recorded in audit log)
curl -sS "https://horizon.example/api/v1/$ORG/nodes" \
  -H "X-Api-Key: nk_live_<base64url>"
  • Key formats: nk_live_<base64url> (production), nk_test_<base64url> (non-production). Keys can carry an expiry and can be revoked.
  • Every request is forced to the key's org: a ?org= override or a mismatching path org returns 403. Only GET is allowed; all mutations return 403.
  • Partners never talk to the Edge Exchange directly — the BFF holds one shared exchange credential, and every call is written to the append-only audit log.
  • The console API (openapi-console.yaml) is a different surface for browser users (Flow C); partners use openapi-partner.yaml only.

docs.title: Flow C — browser user inside the suite (SSO + gateway)
docs.text: When NS is the entry point, the user logs in once and reaches every product without signing in again. Your frontend never handles a password or an upstream token.

docs.title: C.1 Login and the gateway
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Browser
    participant NS as NereidSphere
    participant NI as NereidIdentity
    participant P as Product (NL/NF/NH)
    U->>NS: open portal (no session)
    NS->>NI: authorization-code + PKCE
    NI-->>U: branded login (possibly brokered IdP / MFA)
    U->>NI: authenticate
    NI-->>NS: code → server-side token exchange, verified id token
    NS-->>U: sealed ns_session cookie (HttpOnly, SameSite)
    U->>NS: GET /p/link/v1/tenants/t/devices (cookie)
    NS->>P: forward with X-User-Id / X-User-Email / X-User-Roles
    P-->>U: response

Rules for a client of the gateway:

  • Call products under /p/{product}/...; the prefix is stripped before forwarding (/p/link/v1/… → the NL origin's /v1/…).
  • Credentials are the ns_session cookie — send same-origin/credentialed requests; you do not present a bearer token.
  • Mutating requests carry the double-submit CSRF header X-Csrf-Token, equal to the readable ns_csrf cookie. OPTIONS preflight and the server-to-server ticket exchange are exempt.
  • Never send X-User-* or X-NS-Integration-Secret yourself: inbound copies are always removed, then the gateway stamps the verified values. A product trusts those headers only on requests arriving from the gateway.

docs.title: C.2 Entering a separately hosted product (the ticket)
docs.text:
The browser holds only an NS cookie, so opening an independently hosted product uses a one-time handoff ticket (30-second, single-use, audience-bound):

sequenceDiagram
    participant U as Browser
    participant NS as NereidSphere
    participant P as Product backend
    U->>NS: GET /auth/enter/{product}?to=/dashboard
    NS->>NS: resolve session; require /nereid{product}/{tenant}/{role} group
    NS-->>U: 302 {product.url}/auth/ns-callback?ticket=…&to=/dashboard
    U->>P: GET /auth/ns-callback?ticket=…
    P->>NS: POST /api/v1/auth/ticket/verify<br/>X-NS-Client-Id / X-NS-Client-Secret
    NS-->>P: identity snapshot + "to"
    P-->>U: product-local session

The product backend (not the browser) verifies the ticket:

POST https://sphere.example/api/v1/auth/ticket/verify
X-NS-Client-Id: link
X-NS-Client-Secret: <products[].sso_secret>
Content-Type: application/json

{"ticket":"..."}

The response carries the verified identity — sub, preferred_username, email, name, roles, and groups (suite assignments of the form /nereid{product}/{tenant}/{role}) — plus the relative to path. Products are default-deny: a user without an assignment group for that product is redirected back to the portal; a valid identity alone is not enough. The product then mints its own normal session (NF, for example, issues its local JWT and resolves the tenant for X-Tenant-Id).

docs.title: C.3 Alternative for an ingress: external-auth
docs.text: A product/ingress that must not implement the ticket exchange can delegate authentication to GET https://<ns>/api/v1/auth/verify (ingress external-auth). A valid session returns 204 plus the X-User-* response headers to forward; trust those headers only on the authenticated path.

docs.title: Flow D — device and gateway firmware
docs.text:
Physical devices and edge gateways do not use user accounts or OAuth. They authenticate with a device credential provisioned in NL and speak the southbound wire protocol:

  • Credential: access token (MQTT username), id + secret (Basic), or mutual TLS (X.509).
  • Transport: MQTT topics (v1/me/* for direct devices, v1/gateway/* after hello for gateways) or HTTP (/v1/me/telemetry, /v1/me/blob, long-poll commands).
  • Gateways additionally negotiate hello/heartbeat/manifest and relay sub-device traffic.

This is a full flow of its own — start with the Device SDK (Go), Direct device integration and Gateway integration. Binary telemetry (images/documents into S3) is documented at Binary media and S3 storage. Adding a new southbound protocol to the platform itself uses the Adapter SDK.

docs.title: Flow E — standalone product against your IdP (direct OIDC)
docs.text:
A product sold/deployed without the suite portal can be a standard OIDC relying party directly against NI (which may broker your corporate IdP):

  1. Register a confidential/public client for the product with a fixed redirect URI; ROPC is disabled, so use authorization-code + PKCE.
  2. Discover endpoints from https://<issuer>/auth/realms/nereidai/.well-known/openid-configuration.
  3. Complete the code exchange server side, verify the id token against JWKS (issuer, audience, expiry, nonce), and build the product's own session.
  4. Resolve product-local authorization from the suite role/group claims; the product remains the authority for its own RBAC.

In suite deployments this is the oidc integration mode, while every other product typically stays on the default ns ticket mode. NS and the product must agree on the mode — a mismatch is the usual cause of login loops. Details and claim mapping: SSO & OIDC.

docs.title: Decision checklist
docs.text:
1. Is there an interactive user? No → A (NL) or B (NH); Yes → C (suite) or E (standalone).
  2. Is the caller firmware? → always D.
  3. Does the integration need writes to edge exchange? The NH partner API is read-only; operational writes go through the console/API as an authenticated user, not a partner key.
  4. Confirm the deployment shape: suite (gateway + tickets exist) or standalone (direct origins + direct OIDC).
  5. Provision credentials out of band with the operator: service account, partner key, OIDC client, or device credential. None are self-registered.

docs.text:

  • SSO & OIDC · RBAC
  • Embedded OpenAPI: NS and NL serve an offline Swagger UI at /api/docs; NH ships console and partner specs; NF ships docs/api/openapi.yaml.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
NereidAI is open source under the Apache License 2.0, developed across a set of independent repositories under the NereidAI GitHub organization. This page describes how to engage at a high level; the authoritative detail lives in each repository.

Developer documentation

Contribution rules, exact commands and review expectations are owned by each repository. Start from the NereidAI organization and read that repository's own contributing guide and operating rules first.

docs.title: Where to engage
docs.text:
Every product is its own repository with its own issue tracker. Use the product repository that owns the area you are touching — a fix in the wrong repository is not a license to fix it elsewhere.

Repo (GitHub org) Owns Sphere Portal, unified API gateway, cross-product event glue. Identity Suite SSO / identity federation. Link IoT pipeline: device access, rules, alerts, dashboards. Forge Model factory: datasets, training, export, registry. Horizon Edge distribution and rollout. Edge Southbound edge integration on field gateways. Fleet Robot fleet management. Mobile Mobile app and WeChat Mini Program.

Discussion happens through GitHub issues and Discussions — that is the community support channel. For enterprise questions, see Community & Support.

docs.title: The contribution flow
docs.text:
1. Pick the owning repository and read its README, contributing guide and operating rules.
  2. Open or find an issue describing the change before large work, so scope is agreed in the open.
  3. Branch, implement, and verify in that repository using its own format / lint / type-check / test / build commands — never invent scripts a project does not have.
  4. Open a pull request with a clear description; keep each change focused and reviewable.

One change, one repository

Sibling repositories are treated as read-only from any single repository's work. A cross-repo fix is handed to the owning repository as a coordinated change, not applied sideways.

docs.title: Commit and authorship conventions
docs.text:
• Conventional Commits. Prefix messages with a type such as feat:, fix:, chore: or docs:.

  • DCO sign-off. Every commit carries a Signed-off-by line; use git commit -s.

    git commit -s

  • One verified milestone per commit. Stage only intended files, and commit a stage once it is verified rather than in one large batch.

docs.title: License header
docs.text:
Every hand-written source file (Go, Python, TS/TSX, SQL, authored YAML, proto, shell) must start with the project header, in the comment syntax of the language:

// Copyright (C) 2026 YIQISOFT
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

Vendored code is different

Vendored / third-party subtrees follow upstream conventions — upstream license headers, formatting and workflow. Do not add or revert headers there. The header rule applies only to hand-written NereidAI code.

docs.title: Verify before you finish
docs.text: Never finish on "edited successfully" — finish on "verified". Run the owning repository's formatting, lint, type-check, tests and build, and fix every failure. Note that front-end bundler builds do not type-check on their own, so run the project's type checker separately. Clean up any test processes and temporary files you created. The exact commands are listed in the repository.

docs.title: Versioning and contracts
docs.text:
• A repository-level VERSION file is the release source of truth and the source of derived image tags; do not change it without an explicit request.
  • When a public API, request/response shape, WebSocket frame or wire contract changes, update the specification and the affected docs in the same change.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started — orient yourself in the suite.
  • Conventions — the shared coding conventions.
  • Cross-Product Contracts — what the suite fixes.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
The suite shares a small set of conventions that hold across every product repository. This page is a concise, upper-layer summary — the authoritative detail lives in the repositories, in each product's operating rules and its own contributor documentation.

Developer documentation

Treat this as orientation, not as the rulebook. The binding version of every convention below is defined in the repository. Start from the NereidAI organization.

docs.title: Language and comments
docs.text:
• Comments are English only. Chinese comments in source are not allowed.
  • Every file has a module/package-level comment describing what it does, its architectural role, and important invariants.
  • Doc comments start with the identifier name. Every exported function, method, type, interface and constant carries a doc comment beginning with the identifier it documents; non-trivial unexported code is commented too.
  • Comments explain why — intent, invariants, ordering, workarounds — not a restatement of the code.

docs.title: License header
docs.text:
Every hand-written source file (Go, Python, TS/TSX, SQL, authored YAML, proto, shell) begins with the project header, using the language's comment syntax:

// Copyright (C) 2026 YIQISOFT
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

Generated files are exempt only where the generator controls the header; vendored / third-party subtrees keep their upstream headers and follow upstream conventions.

docs.title: Change discipline
docs.text:
The simplest complete solution wins, and the order of preference for every change is Delete > Replace > Add:

  • Solve problems at the owner of the behaviour rather than guarding a symptom.
  • Search the repository before adding anything; reuse or extend what exists.
  • Keep scope minimal — no speculative flags, shims or unrelated cleanup.
  • Keep one authoritative definition per fact (defaults, labels, image tags) and align every copy in the same change.

docs.title: API and data conventions
docs.text: Convention Rule API specification Public APIs are described with OpenAPI 3.1; the spec moves in the same change as the code, and must parse. Empty arrays Arrays are emitted as [], never null. Clients may rely on the shape. No invented semantics The platform never guesses meaning — e.g. units come only from user-defined descriptors. Neutral contracts Wire contracts and platform APIs stay protocol-, stack-, and vendor-agnostic. Migrations Schema changes ship as explicit, numbered, reversible (paired up/down) migrations — never auto-mutated at startup.

docs.title: Internationalization
docs.text:
• No hardcoded user-facing strings. Every label and message goes through the project's translation mechanism (t(...)).
  • Both locales move together. New keys land in the English and Chinese locales in the same change, and the project's i18n check runs as part of it.
  • Operator-visible behaviour is documented in both languages' help docs in the same change.

docs.title: Language and stack (confirmed)
docs.text:
Where a convention is language-specific, it follows the product's own stack:

  • Go services use the standard library net/http (Sphere) and pgx for PostgreSQL access (Link).
  • Python services use FastAPI (Forge, and Fleet's planned platform API).

These are orientation notes only; each repository documents the exact libraries, versions and tooling it uses.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Getting Started — orient yourself in the suite.
  • Contributing — how to engage with the repositories.
  • Cross-Product Contracts — the contract rules.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
NereidAI is an end-to-end AIoT platform delivered as a suite of focused products. Every product is an independent repository under the NereidAI GitHub organization, and together they form one closed loop — with no mandatory cloud dependency. See the Suite Overview for what each product does, and the Architecture Overview for how the pieces fit.

Developer documentation

This page orients you; the product repositories are authoritative for setup, exact commands and internals. Start from the NereidAI organization and read the product's README first.

docs.title: One suite, independent repositories
docs.text:
The suite layer federates the domain products but never absorbs their logic. Each product owns its own UI, APIs and release cycle, and carries its own quick-start guide in its README.

Product Role Sphere Thin suite layer — single portal, unified API gateway, cross-product event glue. Identity Suite SSO and identity center — OIDC / LDAP / SAML federation, RBAC. Link Privatized IoT data pipeline — device access, rules, alerts, dashboards. Forge Model factory — datasets, training, optimization, multi-silicon export. Horizon Edge distribution — policy-driven rollout, bandwidth-aware delivery, OTA. Edge Southbound edge integration on field gateways — zero-touch, mTLS, autonomy. Fleet Robot fleet management — task scheduling, traffic control, teleoperation. Mobile Operator's mobile window into Link — app and WeChat Mini Program.

Independently deployable

Every domain product can run standalone; nothing requires the others to start. The suite services (Sphere, Identity) are optional for single-product deployments, and are thin layers that never duplicate a product's features.

flowchart LR
    EDGE["NE\nfield gateways"]
    LINK["NL\nIoT pipeline"]
    FORGE["NF\nmodel factory"]
    HORIZON["NH\nedge distribution"]

    EDGE -->|mTLS telemetry| LINK
    LINK -->|datasets| FORGE
    FORGE -->|models / apps| HORIZON
    HORIZON -->|OTA| EDGE

docs.title: Find your product's quick start
docs.text: Open the repository for the product you care about and follow its README (and any INSTALL / docs guide it links). Link ships one codebase in two forms — an all-in-one binary or Kubernetes microservices; Edge runs on field gateways; the newer products (Fleet, Mobile) are early stage, so check the repository for current scope.

docs.title: Run it yourself
docs.text:
A couple of representative entry points, one per product family. Treat these as signposts — the product repository holds the full command set.

SphereLinkHorizon 
make dev          # run the backend (configs/dev.yaml)
make web-dev      # Vite dev server with hot reload

make build        # web build + self-contained binary

make dev-all      # PostgreSQL container + backend + frontend

Maturity varies

Products sit at different gates. Verify the current status in the product repository rather than assuming a stable interface everywhere — see the Roadmap.

docs.title: Connect a device
docs.text:
• Field devices → Edge → Link. Edge runs on a field gateway and bridges southbound devices into Link over the gateway MQTT protocol, with mTLS and store-and-forward buffering.
  • Direct devices → Link. Link accepts MQTT, HTTP and CoAP through one shared envelope and SDK, so behaviour is identical across transports.
Adding a new southbound protocol

New protocols are added with the Link Adapter SDK, as a separate project or repository that translates a wire protocol into platform contracts. The SDK lives under sdk/ in the Link repository, ships an annotated skeleton (adapters/template) and a full reference adapter (adapters/coap), and never requires importing internal/ packages.

docs.title: Getting Started with NereidEdge
docs.text:
NereidEdge is an EdgeX Foundry application service that bridges field devices into Link. It converts EdgeX events and readings into Link gateway telemetry frames over the gateway MQTT protocol, mapping EdgeX device names to Link sub-devices. It runs on a field gateway alongside an EdgeX 4.0.2 stack.

Stands alone with Link

Edge needs only a reachable Link broker and gateway credentials. It does not require Sphere or Horizon to run. Horizon is how Edge is distributed and kept up to date across many sites, not a runtime dependency.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• An EdgeX Foundry 4.0.2 stack running on the gateway (core services, the NATS message bus and device services).
  • A reachable Link MQTT broker (tcp:// or tls://).
  • Link gateway credentials created in the Link console: Credential ID, credential secret and the gateway's Edge ID — see Gateway Integration for the platform side and the gateway concept.
  • Each field device already registered in Link as a sub-device bound to the gateway, so its sub-device UUID is known.

docs.title: 1. Prepare the platform side
docs.text: In the Link console, create a gateway device, add a gateway credential, and register each field device as a sub-device bound to that gateway. Note every sub-device UUID; Edge maps EdgeX device names to them. Reading the Gateway Integration handshake (hello, heartbeat and manifest) first makes Edge logs much easier to follow.

docs.title: 2. Configure the device map
docs.text:
Edit the EdgeX custom configuration file res/configuration.yaml under the NereidEdge section:

NereidEdge:
  BrokerURL: "tcp://<link-mqtt-host>:1883"
  CredentialID: "<your-cred-id>"
  CredentialSecret: "<your-cred-secret>"
  EdgeID: "<edge-instance-id>"
  DeviceMap: "edgex-device-1:<link-subdevice-uuid-1>,edgex-device-2:<link-subdevice-uuid-2>"

DeviceMap is a comma-separated list of edgex-device-name:link-subdevice-uuid pairs. In production use a tls:// broker URL and keep the credential secret in a secrets manager rather than committing it to a file.

docs.title: 3. Build and run
docs.text: Build the binary with make build-local or the container image with make docker, then run Edge as an EdgeX application service — bare metal, Docker, or Docker Compose joined to the EdgeX network. On startup Edge performs the Link hello/feature negotiation and then begins relaying telemetry. The deployment modes, networking and compose details live in the product repository's docs/deployment.md.

docs.title: 4. Verify the bridge
docs.text:
1. Check the Edge service health endpoint: GET /api/v4/ping on port 59750 returns pong.
  2. In the Link console the gateway and its mapped sub-devices show Online. Edge attaches a sub-device on its first telemetry and sends a full device manifest every five minutes.
  3. Open a sub-device and confirm its readings update — EdgeX readings now appear as Link telemetry keyed by the mapped UUID.

If no data arrives, verify the DeviceMap pairs, that EdgeX events reach the application service over the message bus, and that the gateway credential and Edge ID pass negotiation.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Gateway Integration — the northbound contract Edge speaks.
  • NereidEdge product page and Edge delivery.
  • Configuration, troubleshooting and the protocol reference live in the NereidEdge repository (NereidAI).

docs.title: Getting Started with NereidFleet
docs.text:
Tech Preview — design stage

Fleet is at an early design stage (v0.1 draft). The repository currently holds design documents, research and proposed architecture decisions rather than a runnable product; there is no operator console to install yet. This guide describes the intended first-run path and today's simulation proof of concept, not a finished workflow.

NereidFleet is the planned management, control and collaboration platform for embodied-AI robot fleets — wheeled AMRs, quadruped, humanoid and balancing robots. It will provide a robot roster with live status, multi-robot task dispatch and traffic coordination, teleoperation and emergency stop, built on an open stack: ROS 2, Eclipse Zenoh, Open-RMF and EdgeX Foundry.

docs.title: What it will do
docs.text:
• Management — asset ledger, fleet grouping, edge-node management, maps, permissions and audit.
  • Control — single-robot teleoperation, emergency stop, safety-mode switching, and real-time state and telemetry.
  • Collaboration — multi-robot task orchestration, traffic control, conflict resolution and cross-robot cooperation.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text:
There is nothing for operators to deploy in the Tech Preview. The project follows a simulation-first, hardware-second route, and the engineering milestones are:

  1. Phase 0 — simulation (no hardware): bring up the validated Free Fleet multi-robot example with Open-RMF and a Zenoh ROS 2 DDS bridge, and verify task dispatch and traffic negotiation end to end.
  2. Phase 1 — wheeled-robot PoC: adapt one wheeled AMR (the first target platform), put at least two robots on one Zenoh bus, and stand up a minimal roster/task/telemetry API and web UI.
  3. Phase 2 — edge and northbound: connect EdgeX, research VDA5050 over MQTT for cloud-master scenarios, and extend to quadruped and humanoid robots.

The recommended environment for the simulation phase is Ubuntu 24.04 with ROS 2 Jazzy, the Cyclone DDS RMW, Zenoh 1.5 or newer, and Open-RMF. Closed-loop integration with the Edge → Forge → Horizon → Link pipeline is future work.

Safety stays on the vehicle

A platform emergency stop is never the only stop path. Every robot must keep a vehicle-side hardware E-stop or independent safety loop that can halt it during a network or bus failure.

docs.title: Stay informed
docs.text:
• NereidFleet product page — target design and key facts.
  • Roadmap — maturity across the suite.
  • The research reports, feasibility study and proposed ADRs live in the NereidFleet repository (NereidAI); check it for current scope before planning any integration.

docs.title: Annotations
docs.text:
Annotations turn raw data into labeled training sets. Forge does not rebuild a labeling tool: it integrates Label Studio (images, text and conversation) and CVAT (video and tracking) as embedded workbenches, and adds a self-built ML Backend that pre-labels with your own models. The intended division of labor is the machine labels first, a human reviews and corrects.

In an internal run on 128 street-scene images (8 classes), one pre-labeling pass produced 269 boxes on 75 images — about 59% of the images needed no boxes drawn from scratch. Your savings depend on the model and scene; measure them on a pilot batch.

docs.title: Task types
docs.text: Workbench Tasks Label Studio (images) Object detection (rectangles), segmentation (polygons/masks), classification, keypoints, oriented boxes Label Studio (text) Text classification, named entities, generation/chat review CVAT (video) Object tracking across frames, keyframe interpolation, click-to-segment

docs.title: Flow
docs.text:
1. Create a project — on the Annotations page, pick a dataset version and the task type; the project carries the label schema (the class list).
  2. Open the workbench — the tool is embedded; images or text open directly, they are not copied (the workbench references presigned object URLs).
  3. Choose a pre-labeling model — in the project header select a registered model version (detection/segmentation; SAM is offered separately in the video editor). The choice is remembered per project.
  4. Run semi-automated annotation — the ML Backend predicts on the unlabeled tasks and writes predictions as editable drafts in the workbench.
  5. Review and correct — a human confirms, fixes or discards each draft.
  6. Export — the export becomes a new, immutable dataset version.

docs.title: Pre-labeling models
docs.text:
The ML Backend is model-agnostic; it routes by model family:

  • CNN models (YOLO / RT-DETR for detection, SAM for segmentation, classifiers) run through ONNX Runtime / Triton.
  • VLM models (for example Qwen-VL / Florence-2) run through a vLLM-compatible OpenAI endpoint and turn prompts into labels or boxes — useful for irregular categories and zero-shot first passes.
  • Trained models loop back: after a model is trained, selecting that model version for pre-labeling makes subsequent batches faster (the flywheel).

Suggestions below the project's confidence threshold are left unlabeled for a human rather than inserted as noisy boxes. See ML Backend for service registration and health.

docs.title: Video to training frames
docs.text:
CVAT labels video with tracks and keyframes; trainers consume frame images. Forge provides a built-in video frame-extraction pipeline component:

CVAT export (tracks / keyframes / boxes)
   ──► extract at chosen fps / sampling (uniform or activity-based)
   ──► interpolate labels between keyframes
   ──► frame images + regenerated COCO/YOLO labels
   ──► new dataset version (extracted once, reusable for many runs)

You do not extract frames by hand; the extraction runs as a preparation step, and the extracted frames can be reused by later training runs.

docs.title: Review and quality
docs.text:
• Treat pre-labels as drafts: spot-check a sample before exporting, especially when the class list changed or the model is weak.
  • Keep the model's class space identical to the project's label schema — mismatched classes are the usual reason predictions look empty or wrong.
  • Export only reviewed work; the exported version is immutable and is what the trainer consumes.

docs.title: Export formats
docs.text: Data Export Images (detection / segmentation) COCO, YOLO (plus Label Studio JSON / CSV from the workbench) Text classification Plain JSONL (text,label) Generation / chat Sharegpt JSONL — directly usable by LLM-SFT training Video Frame images + COCO/YOLO via the frame-extraction component

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Pre-labeling returns nothing or is disabled?

A model version must be selected in the project header (and have weights available); the button is disabled until then. If predictions run but look empty, verify the model's classes match the project labels and lower the confidence threshold. A weak model returning few suggestions is normal on the first batch.

Where does the export go?

It becomes a new dataset version (YOLO/COCO for vision, JSONL for text), immediately selectable on the Training page.

Labels and model classes disagree?

Re-export with an aligned label schema, or choose the model version trained on those same classes.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Training — start a CV or LLM/VLM run from the exported version.
  • ML Backend — register or troubleshoot the pre-labeling service.
  • Datasets — how versions are stored and reused.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text: Datasets are the starting point of every Forge workflow. A dataset is a versioned container: every upload and every annotation export creates a new, immutable version, and every training, optimization or evaluation job references one exact version. That is what makes every model reproducible.

docs.title: Dataset formats
docs.text:
Choose the format that matches the model family:

Format Used for Contents COCO CV detection / segmentation Images + a COCO annotations.json YOLO CV training Images + YOLO labels + data.yaml ImageNet Image classification Per-class folder layout LLM-SFT LLM / VLM fine-tuning A sharegpt-style JSONL corpus; VLM datasets additionally carry an images/ folder JSONL Text corpora One sample per line (plain text, {text}, {data} or sharegpt conversations)
